25.0.s.en: 1. God, the Possessor of authority and the Giver of peace in heaven

25.0.0.en: 1 Then answered Bildad the Shuhite, and said, 2 "Dominion and fear are with him, he maketh peace in his high places. 3 Is there any number of his armies? and upon whom doth not his light arise?

25.0.1.en: Then answered Bildad the Shuhite, and said: [1]

25.1.1.en: What Bildad uttered is a truth befitting God and us, namely that it is fitting for us to humble ourselves greatly before the exalted and awesome God, and that the distance between Him and us is vast. But Bildad erred in applying this to Job, since he did not bear toward him a spirit of love.

25.1.2.en: God, as the Creator of heaven and earth, the Creator of all and the Giver of life, has the absolute right to lay down laws and to govern the universe with absolute authority. As Nebuchadnezzar said when he returned to his senses and blessed the Most High: "His dominion is an everlasting dominion, and his kingdom is from generation to generation: and all the inhabitants of the earth are reputed as nothing: and he doeth according to his will in the army of heaven, and among the inhabitants of the earth: and none can stay his hand, or say unto him, What doest thou?" (Dan 4:34-35).

25.1.3.en: With the great boldness that the men of God had toward Him, they confessed that He is the great, mighty, awesome and fearful God.

25.1.4.en: "Let them praise thy great and terrible name; for it is holy" (Ps 99:3).

25.1.5.en: "And I prayed unto the Lord my God, and made my confession, and said, O Lord, the great and dreadful God, keeping the covenant and mercy to them that love him, and to them that keep his commandments" (Dan 9:4).

25.1.6.en: "And said, I beseech thee, O Lord God of heaven, the great and terrible God, that keepeth covenant and mercy for them that love him and observe his commandments" (Neh 1:5).

25.1.7.en: "Now therefore, our God, the great, the mighty, and the terrible God, who keepest covenant and mercy, let not all the trouble seem little before thee, that hath come upon us, on our kings, on our princes, and on our priests, and on our prophets, and on our fathers, and on all thy people, since the time of the kings of Assyria unto this day" (Neh 9:32).

25.1.8.en: Commenting on Psalm 99, which speaks of God sitting between the cherubim, the awesome One before whom the peoples tremble and the earth is moved, St. Augustine sees Him seated upon the human soul, enthroned there as upon His holy throne.

25.1.9.en: * The Cherubim is the seat of God, as Holy Scripture shows us, a high heavenly throne that we do not see, but the Word of God knows it; He knows it as His seat... God does not sit as man sits. But if you wish God to sit in you, then if you become good you become a seat for God... The soul of the righteous is the seat of wisdom. For a throne in our language is called a seat... Because God is exalted above all knowledge, it is said of Him that He sits upon the fullness of knowledge. Let there be in you the fullness of knowledge, and you will become the throne of God... And when you have the fullness of knowledge and have love, you become the throne of God, and you become a heaven. For the heaven that we look at with these eyes of ours is not very precious to God. Holy souls are the heaven of God, the minds of the angels, and all the minds of His servants are the heaven of God.

25.1.10.en: St. Augustine "He maketh peace in his high places" [2].

25.1.11.en: If men in their stubbornness or wickedness resist God, they only resist themselves, for they lose the surpassing peace of God. But the heavenly ones enjoy His peace in the heights, since they love Him and submit to Him and obey Him with perfect obedience. They bear the divine love and imitate His humility, so they do not exalt themselves over one another, nor envy, nor quarrel, nor murmur. It is God's surpassing gift to them, as those who love Him, to live in wondrous peace.

25.1.12.en: As for the inhabitants of the earth, they need obedience to God, so that they may enjoy His work as the Giver of peace, as the psalmist says: "He maketh the storm a calm, so that the waves thereof are still" (Ps 107:29; 65:7).

25.1.13.en: Pope Gregory (the Great) sees that God, as the Creator of all things, reigns over them and has authority, striking awe into the hearts of mortal creation. On earth creation lacks peace, and confusion and anxiety come upon them; but in the heights, or in the heavenly world, God unites the elect with the orders of angels, and all are at peace.

25.1.14.en: In the Lord we are transformed from earthly dust into heavens, and are reckoned His high places, where He dwells in us and establishes our peace within us. As the Apostle says: "For he is our peace, who hath made both one, and hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us" (Eph 2:14).

25.1.15.en: * Since Christ, the Son of God, is peace, He came to gather together those who are His, and to separate them from the wicked.

25.1.16.en: St. Augustine * "Peace I leave with you" (Jn 14:27). He says: "What harm can the troubles of the world do you, so long as you are at peace with me? For this peace is not of the same kind as that (which is of the world). That is an outward peace, often harmful and of no profit, with no advantage to those who possess it. But I give them a peace of the kind by which you are at peace with one another, and which makes you stronger."

25.1.17.en: St. John Chrysostom * "Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord": the King against the tyrant, who came not by showing that He is almighty and all-wise, but by what was reckoned as the foolishness of the Cross, by which He rescued those who are His from the captives held by the serpent, wise in evil.

25.1.18.en: "Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord": the Truth against the liar, the Savior against the destroyer, the Prince of Peace against the instigator of wars, the Lover of mankind against the hater of humanity.

25.1.19.en: "Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord," the Lord who comes to have mercy on the creature, the work of His hands.

25.1.20.en: "Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord," the Lord who comes to save man who had gone astray in error, to remove error from him, to give light to those who are in darkness, to abolish the deceit of idols and put in its place the knowledge of God, the Giver of salvation, so that the world may be sanctified. He removes the abominations and the misery that belong to the worship of false gods.

25.1.21.en: Father Methodius ascribes the high heavens to Himself, for the heavens are the Lord's (Ps 115:16), and Bildad calls them "his high places."

25.1.22.en: When the people are sanctified, the Lord ascribes the people and their feasts to Himself, so that it is called "the people of God," "my sabbaths," etc.; and when it rebels, He calls it "the people," "your feasts," "your sabbaths," etc.

25.2.0.en: "Is there any number of his armies? and upon whom doth not his light arise?" [3]

25.2.1.en: The peace that dwells in the Lord's heights or heavens is not because the number of the heavenly ones is small, so that agreement and harmony might be reached among them, for "is there any number of his armies?" Rather, the secret of their peace in the Lord is that He shines with His light upon all of them. If the light of the sun reaches the whole earth, the light of God shines upon all the heavenly ones [and upon whom doth not his light arise?]

25.2.2.en: Thus He who shines with His light upon all the heavenly ones makes His sun to rise on the evil and the good (Mt 5:45), that all may seek the light of His surpassing grace and be enlightened, and bear His righteousness and His peace! He hides His light from no one, and does not begrudge His creation His knowledge, but He does not compel anyone to accept His grace.

25.2.3.en: The Lord Christ calls us to be children of God, saying: "That ye may be the children of your Father which is in heaven: for he maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust" (Mt 5:45). He wants all to be children of light. "For God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ" (2 Cor 4:6).

25.2.4.en: * "For ye were sometimes darkness, but now are ye light in the Lord" (Eph 5:8). He did not say "by your virtue," but by the grace of God working in you. That is, you deserved punishments, and now you are no longer so. Therefore walk as children of light... in all goodness.

25.2.5.en: St. John Chrysostom * Those who were born again were children of night and became children of day; they were darkness and became light. Now Jesus entrusts Himself to them, and they come to Him not by night like Nicodemus (Jn 3:2), nor do they seek Him in the dark but in the day.

25.2.6.en: St. Augustine * By the Holy Spirit our return to Paradise is accomplished, our ascent to the Kingdom of Heaven, our return to adoption as sons, our freedom by which we call God our Father, our fellowship in the grace of Christ, our calling children of light, our fellowship in eternal glory, and in short our attaining to the state of the fullness of blessing.

25.3.s.en: 2. How can man be justified with God?

25.3.0.en: "How then can man be justified with God? or how can he be clean that is born of a woman?" [4]

25.3.1.en: However much the righteousness and holiness of man may rise, it cannot be compared with the loftiness of the righteousness and holiness of God (Ps 89:6). And if man enters into judgment with God, God is justified and man is condemned, as the psalmist says: "And enter not into judgment with thy servant: for in thy sight shall no man living be justified" (Ps 143:2). There is no error in the judgments of God, and no one can object to them or appeal against them.

25.3.2.en: * [Can a man be justified when compared with God? or can one born of a woman be found clean?] [4] This statement was spoken before by the blessed Job... since every man is righteous through being enlightened by God, not by comparison with God. For the righteousness of man, when compared with the Creator, is not reckoned righteousness; for even if man holds fast to his state in creation, the creature cannot be equal to the Creator.

25.3.3.en: In any case, this creature came to carry heavy burdens, and because of his weakness sin piled up upon him, that sin which the serpent brought into him by deceit, and the woman proved her weakness sufficiently. Now, since man is born through a woman subject to sin, he inherited the weakness of the first sin by procreation, not because the branch of the human race was corrupted at its root and did not receive the vitality proper to its creation; therefore it is rightly said now: "Can a man be justified, being born of a woman?"

25.3.4.en: As if he said plainly: Let no man think proudly against his Creator; let him consider from where he came to this place, and understand what he is.

25.3.5.en: But observe that there are those who have received help by the gift of the Spirit against the frailty of their flesh, and have built themselves up, and shone in the virtues. Yes! They shine in wondrous and astonishing signs. Yet there is no man who passes through life without sin, so long as he bears the corruptible flesh.

25.3.7.en: * Who are those who desire to enter into judgment with Him but those who are ignorant of God's righteousness, and wish to establish their own righteousness...? "In thy sight shall no man living be justified." "Every man living" here means one who lives in the flesh, who lives expecting death. He is born as a man, received his life from a man, came from Adam... He can be justified before himself, but not before You. How is he justified before himself? By pleasing himself and not pleasing You. Enter not into judgment with me, O Lord my God. However upright I may seem to myself, when You bring out a standard from Your storehouses by which I measure myself, I find myself crooked.

25.3.8.en: * [Thou art justified in thy sayings, and overcomest when thou art judged] (Ps 51:4). You overcome all men, all judges; whoever thinks himself righteous before You is not righteous. You alone judge justly, and You are judged unjustly... You overcome all men, because You are above all men, and they were created by You.

25.4.s.en: 3. The stars are not pure in his sight

25.4.0.en: 5 "Behold even the moon, and it shineth not; and the stars are not pure in his sight. 6 How much less man, that is rottenness, and the son of man, which is a worm?"

25.4.1.en: "Behold even the moon, and it shineth not; and the stars are not pure in his sight" [5].

25.4.2.en: Despite the beauty of the moon and all the stars, in reality they are stones that carry neither light nor beauty in themselves, were the rays of the sun not reflected upon them. So it is with the Church, that is, the moon, and the believers also, that is, the stars: they have no beauty except by the shining of the Sun of Righteousness upon them, to scatter every trace of darkness and reflect His splendor upon them. It is said of the true believers and preachers: "And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever" (Dan 12:3).

25.4.3.en: Apart from the grace of God the moon becomes dark, unable to give light, and the stars are reckoned impure. As the prophet Isaiah says: "Then the moon shall be confounded, and the sun ashamed, when the Lord of hosts shall reign in mount Zion, and in Jerusalem" (Isa 24:23).

25.4.4.en: Origen sees that the moon and the stars here refer to rational beings to whom the Lord issues commandments (Isa 12:45), who are capable of advancing as well as of falling.

25.4.5.en: * What does he mean by the moon but the whole Church together, and what does he mean by the stars but the souls of the many who live uprightly? In the midst of the practices of wicked men they stand out by their rare virtues, as though shining in the darkness of the night. So Paul also says to his disciples: [Among whom ye shine as lights in the world] (Phil 15:2). And by the title "stars" he means the elect; Paul tells us this again when he says: [One star differeth from another star in glory] (1 Cor 41:15). So "the moon shineth not, and the stars are not pure in his sight." The Holy Church does not by her own power shine in so many wonders, unless the showers of strengthening grace fall upon her, nor are the minds of the many who live uprightly pure from the defilement of sinful practices, if they were judged apart from (divine) tenderness. For in the eyes of the strict Judge every individual is defiled through his inclination to corruption, unless the grace of (God) removes man day by day from this fall.

25.4.7.en: * Let your ears listen from now to the glorious voice with which the angels will sing because of your salvation, saying: "Blessed is he whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered." This is when you enter as the shining stars of the Church, radiant in body and bright in soul.

25.4.8.en: Great is the baptism that is granted to you, for it is the release of captives, the forgiveness of transgressions, the death of sin, the new birth of the soul, a garment of light, a holy seal that cannot be broken, a chariot to the heavens, the delight of Paradise, a welcome into the Kingdom, the gift of adoption! But beware, for there is a serpent outside watching those who pass by. Be careful lest it bite you with the bites of unbelief.

25.4.9.en: When it sees many receiving salvation, it seeks to swallow it from them (1 Pet 5:8).

25.4.10.en: St. Cyril of Jerusalem * There is never one who is without sin. [The stars themselves are not pure in his sight], and every creature trembles at the coming of the Lord... There is another interpretation, which is that "all" does not refer to everyone but to those who are the subject of the dispute. It is as when someone says: "All the citizens cried out"; he does not mean by this that there was never anyone silent, but this was said of the majority that prevails over the minority.

25.4.11.en: St. Jerome * No man is without sin, whether his life is one day or he lives many years. If the stars themselves are not pure in the eyes of God, how much more the worm and corruption, which is what those have become who were subject to the sin of Adam's disobedience?

25.4.12.en: St. Augustine * Is He not good who lifted the earth to a heaven, so that the shining stars that accompany Him reflect His glory in heaven as in a mirror, just as the ranks of the apostles, the martyrs and the priests shine like glorious stars, and give light to the world?

25.5.0.en: "How much less man, that is rottenness, and the son of man, which is a worm." [6]

25.5.1.en: If man returns to his origin before creation and withdraws from God his Creator, he goes as dust and ashes, rottenness and a worm! And the wonder is that the divine Word in His incarnation humbled Himself greatly, and said by the mouth of the prophet: [I am a worm, and no man] (Ps 22:6).

25.5.2.en: * All men are born of flesh; what are they but worms? Out of this worm God makes angels. If the Lord Himself says: "But I am a worm, and no man" (Ps 6:22), who will hesitate to utter what is written in Job: "How much less man, that is rottenness, and the son of man, which is a worm" [6]. He said first "man is rottenness," and then "the son of man is a worm," for the worm comes out of rottenness... Behold what He wished to become for your sake, He who "in the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God" (Jn 1:1).

25.5.3.en: St. Augustine * "How much more is man corruption, and the son of man a worm?" [6] As if he said plainly: If these very persons cannot avoid the contagion, who in the darkness of the present life shine with the splendor of the acquisition of virtues, how great then is the evil of those bound to life according to the flesh? If these persons cannot be freed from sin, who are already walking in the way of heavenly desires, what of those who still lie under the burdens of evil habits, who are abandoned to the pleasures of their bodies and still bear the yoke of corruption? Therefore Peter says: [If the righteous scarcely be saved, where shall the ungodly and the sinner appear?] (1 Pet 18:4). Isaiah says: [Upon the land of my people shall come up thorns and briers; yea, upon all the houses of joy in the joyous city] (Isa 13:32)... The joyous city is the mind of the wicked, who does not care about the punishments to come, for the sake of the pleasure of the flesh, and when the mind goes out of its own being it plays in false merriment.

25.5.5.en: Pope Gregory observes that the first man is called corruption, since death came upon him through sin and he was corrupted. But the son of man is called a worm, since corruption breeds worms in the dead body.

25.5.6.en: Let the light of Your righteousness shine upon me

25.5.7.en: * You shine with the light of Your love upon all creation.

25.5.8.en: By You the heavenly orders are enlightened, and without You heaven appears impure.

25.5.9.en: By You the heavenly ones live in peace, and without You there is no peace even in heaven. * How shall I be justified before You, when corruption has come upon my depths?

25.5.10.en: Who removes corruption from me but You?

25.5.11.en: Let Your grace work in me, O All-Good!
